1	---
2	title: Upgrade to v1
3	description: Comprehensive guide for upgrading from Prisma 1 to Prisma ORM v1
4	url: /guides/upgrade-prisma-orm/v1
5	metaTitle: 'Upgrade from Prisma 1 to Prisma ORM 2'
6	metaDescription: 'Upgrading your project from Prisma 1 to Prisma ORM 2'
7	
8	---
9	
10	This guide provides a comprehensive roadmap for migrating your project from Prisma 1 to the latest version of Prisma ORM. The migration process involves significant architectural changes and requires careful planning and execution.
11	
12	## Before you begin
13	
14	- **Back up your database** before starting the migration
15	- Review the [Prisma ORM documentation](/orm/v7) to understand the new architecture
16	- Set up a separate development environment for testing the migration
17	- Document your current Prisma 1 setup, including models, relations, and any custom configurations
18	
19	## Key changes
20	
21	### Architectural changes
22	
23	| Feature | Prisma 1 | Prisma ORM |
24	|---------|----------|------------|
25	| **Database Connection** | Uses Prisma Server as a proxy | Direct database connection |
26	| **API** | GraphQL API for database | Programmatic access via Prisma Client |
27	| **Schema** | GraphQL SDL + `prisma.yml` | Unified Prisma schema |
28	| **Modeling** | GraphQL SDL | Prisma Schema Language (PSL) |
29	| **Workflow** | `prisma deploy` | `prisma migrate` and `prisma db` commands |
30	
31	### Feature changes
32	
33	- **Removed**: GraphQL API for database
34	- **New**: Type-safe database client
35	- **Improved**: Database introspection and migration tools
36	- **Enhanced**: Support for more database features and types
37	
38	## Migration Strategy
39	
40	### 1. Preparation
41	
42	#### Install Prisma ORM
43	
44	```npm
45	# Initialize a new project
46	npm init -y
47	npm install prisma@7.10.0 @prisma/client@7.10.0
48	
49	# Initialize Prisma
50	npx prisma init
51	```
52	
53	#### Set up Database Connection
54	
55	Update the `DATABASE_URL` in your `.env` file to point to your existing database:
56	
57	```bash
58	DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/your_database?schema=public"
59	```
60	
61	### 2. Schema Migration
62	
63	#### Introspect Database
64	
65	```npm
66	npx prisma db pull
67	```
68	
69	This will generate a `schema.prisma` file based on your existing database schema.
70	
71	#### Update Schema
72	
73	After introspection, you'll need to make several adjustments to the schema:
74	
75	##### Default Values
76	
77	```prisma
78	// Before (Prisma 1)
79	model User {
80	  id        String   @default(cuid())
81	  email     String   @unique
82	  name      String?
83	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
84	  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
85	}
86	```
87	
88	##### Relations
89	
90	```prisma
91	// Before (Prisma 1)
92	type Post {
93	  id        ID!      @id
94	  title     String!
95	  author    User!    @relation(name: "UserPosts")
96	}
97	
98	// After (Prisma ORM)
99	model Post {
100	  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
101	  title     String
102	  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
103	  authorId  Int
104	}
105	```
106	
107	### 3. Data Model Adjustments
108	
109	#### 3.1 Handling Special Types
110	
111	| Prisma 1 Type | Prisma ORM Equivalent | Notes |
112	|---------------|----------------------|-------|
113	| `ID` | `String @id @default(cuid())` | Add `@id` directive |
114	| `DateTime` | `DateTime` | No change needed |
115	| `Json` | `Json` | No change needed |
116	| `Enum` | `Enum` | Define enums in the schema |
117	
118	#### 3.2 Relation Handling
119	
120	Prisma ORM requires explicit relation fields and foreign keys:
121	
122	```prisma
123	model User {
124	  id    Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
125	  posts Post[]
126	}
127	
128	model Post {
129	  id       Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
130	  title    String
131	  author   User   @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
132	  authorId Int
133	}
134	```
135	
136	### 4. Update Application Code
137	
138	#### 4.1 Replace Prisma 1 Client with Prisma Client
139	
140	```typescript
141	// Before (Prisma 1)
142	import { prisma } from './generated/prisma-client';
143	
144	async function getUser(id: string) {
145	  return prisma.user({ id });
146	}
147	
148	// After (Prisma ORM)
149	import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
150	const prisma = new PrismaClient();
151	
152	async function getUser(id: number) {
153	  return prisma.user.findUnique({
154	    where: { id }
155	  });
156	}
157	```
158	
159	#### 4.2 Update Queries and Mutations
160	
161	##### Fetching Data
162	
163	```typescript
164	// Before (Prisma 1)
165	const user = await prisma.user({ id: 1 });
166	const posts = await prisma.user({ id: 1 }).posts();
167	
168	// After (Prisma ORM)
169	const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
170	  where: { id: 1 },
171	  include: { posts: true }
172	});
173	const posts = user?.posts;
174	```
175	
176	##### Creating Records
177	
178	```typescript
179	// Before (Prisma 1)
180	const newUser = await prisma.createUser({
181	  name: 'Alice',
182	  email: 'alice@example.com'
183	});
184	
185	// After (Prisma ORM)
186	const newUser = await prisma.user.create({
187	  data: {
188	    name: 'Alice',
189	    email: 'alice@example.com'
190	  }
191	});
192	```
193	
194	## Testing and Validation
195	
196	### 1. Test Data Operations
197	
198	Test all CRUD operations to ensure data consistency:
199	
200	```typescript
201	// Test create
202	const user = await prisma.user.create({
203	  data: { name: 'Test', email: 'test@example.com' }
204	});
205	
206	// Test read
207	const foundUser = await prisma.user.findUnique({
208	  where: { id: user.id }
209	});
210	
211	// Test update
212	const updatedUser = await prisma.user.update({
213	  where: { id: user.id },
214	  data: { name: 'Updated Name' }
215	});
216	
217	// Test delete
218	await prisma.user.delete({
219	  where: { id: user.id }
220	});
221	```
222	
223	### 2. Test Relations
224	
225	Verify that all relations work as expected:
226	
227	```typescript
228	// Test relation queries
229	const userWithPosts = await prisma.user.findUnique({
230	  where: { id: 1 },
231	  include: {
232	    posts: true,
233	    profile: true
234	  }
235	});
236	
237	// Test nested writes
238	const userWithNewPost = await prisma.user.create({
239	  data: {
240	    name: 'Bob',
241	    email: 'bob@example.com',
242	    posts: {
243	      create: {
244	        title: 'Hello World',
245	        content: 'This is my first post'
246	      }
247	    }
248	  },
249	  include: {
250	    posts: true
251	  }
252	});
253	```
254	
255	## Handling Special Cases
256	
257	### 1. Real-time Subscriptions
258	
259	Prisma ORM doesn't include built-in real-time subscriptions. Consider these alternatives:
260	
261	#### Option 1: Database Triggers
262	
263	```sql
264	-- PostgreSQL example
265	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_new_post()
266	RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
267	BEGIN
268	  PERFORM pg_notify('new_post', row_to_json(NEW)::text);
269	  RETURN NEW;
270	END;
271	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
272	
273	CREATE TRIGGER new_post_trigger
274	AFTER INSERT ON "Post"
275	FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION notify_new_post();
276	```
277	
278	#### Option 2: Application-Level Events
279	
280	```typescript
281	// Publish event when creating a post
282	const post = await prisma.post.create({
283	  data: {
284	    title: 'New Post',
285	    content: 'Content',
286	    author: { connect: { id: userId }}
287	  }
288	});
289	
290	// Publish event to your pub/sub system
291	await pubsub.publish('POST_CREATED', { postCreated: post });
292	```
293	
294	### 2. Authentication
295	
296	If you were using Prisma 1's built-in authentication, you'll need to implement your own solution:
297	
298	```typescript
299	import { compare } from 'bcryptjs';
300	import { sign } from 'jsonwebtoken';
301	
302	export async function login(email: string, password: string) {
303	  const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { email } });
304	  if (!user) throw new Error('User not found');
305	  
306	  const valid = await compare(password, user.password);
307	  if (!valid) throw new Error('Invalid password');
308	  
309	  const token = sign({ userId: user.id }, process.env.APP_SECRET!);
310	  return { token, user };
311	}
312	```
313	
314	## Migration Tools
315	
316	### Prisma 1 Upgrade CLI
317	
318	The [Prisma 1 Upgrade CLI](https://github.com/prisma/prisma1-upgrade) can help automate parts of the migration:
319	
320	```npm
321	# Install the upgrade CLI
322	npm install -g prisma1-upgrade
323	
324	# Run the upgrade helper
325	prisma1-upgrade
326	```
327	
328	This tool helps with:
329	- Converting your Prisma 1 datamodel to Prisma schema
330	- Identifying potential issues in your schema
331	- Providing migration recommendations
332	
333	## Performance Considerations
334	
335	1. **Connection Pooling**: Configure connection pooling for better performance:
336	   ```typescript
337	   const prisma = new PrismaClient({
338	     log: ['query', 'info', 'warn', 'error'],
339	     datasources: {
340	       db: {
341	         url: process.env.DATABASE_URL + '&connection_limit=20'
342	       }
343	     }
344	   });
345	   ```
346	
347	2. **Query Optimization**: Use `select` to fetch only needed fields:
348	   ```typescript
349	   const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
350	     where: { id: 1 },
351	     select: {
352	       id: true,
353	       name: true,
354	       email: true
355	     }
356	   });
357	   ```
358	
359	## Next Steps
360	
361	- [Prisma ORM Documentation](/orm/v7)
362	- [Prisma Schema Reference](/orm/v7/reference/prisma-schema-reference)
363	- [Prisma Client API Reference](/orm/v7/reference/prisma-client-reference)
364	- [Prisma Migrate Guide](/orm/v7/prisma-migrate)
365	- [Prisma Studio](https://www.prisma.io/studio)
366	
367	## Getting Help
368	
369	If you encounter issues during migration:
370	1. Search the [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues)
371	2. Ask for help in the [Prisma Slack](https://slack.prisma.io/)
372	3. Open a [GitHub Discussion](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/discussions)
373
